claim: A failure-as-certain frame raised the number of reasons people generated (about +30% in Mitchell 1989, second-hand); reason quality or correctness was never measured. Gap search: the Mitchell 1989 abstract reports no +30%; it says time direction had little effect in Exp 1 and that outcome certainty drove longer, more episodic explanations.
agent_test: Count failure causes with and without a failure frame at equal tokens, but score only causes a code check confirms.

claim: The claim of 30% better identification of correct reasons is a restatement (Klein 2007) of a 30% count increase; it is repeated in 2024-2025 papers without primary check. Hill 2012, cited by a 2025 review for reduced overconfidence, is not a premortem study (support-theory unpacking, N=32).
agent_test: Do not use 30% as a prior; measure confirmed-cause yield instead.

claim: A failure-imagined premortem cut plan confidence about twice as much as pros/cons or cons-only (Veinott 2010, N=178 students, 5 conditions); confidence is the outcome, not plan quality.
agent_test: Measure confidence drop and final plan accuracy under premortem vs pros/cons prompts at equal tokens.

claim: Premortem beat brainstorming for experienced professionals on risk quality, plan changes and black-swan finds (Gallop and Bischoff 2016, N=101); no effect sizes, full text unread.
agent_test: Compare premortem vs plain risk-brainstorm prompt on planning tasks with seeded flaws.

claim: Army cadet field test: premortem plan check gave fewer fouls and less fixation than the standard military check (Peabody 2022, N=52); statistics unseen. Abstract confirms N=52 cadets; the thesis page is dated 2017, not 2022.
agent_test: Fixation proxy: repeated identical failed attempts; run a premortem before the retry.

claim: Premortem vs worst-case method: equal counts for familiar plans (N=72), premortem produced more reasons for complex unfamiliar plans (N=82); cause categories differ by method. Abstract confirms N=72 and N=82; counts only, no statistics seen.
agent_test: Run both frames on easy and hard plans; compare cause categories.

claim: No outcome evidence at scale exists for the premortem: pages and reviews say it was never formally evaluated, and a debiasing review found none against overconfidence. Roose 2023 (10 game teams, n=68) had no control arm and few teams revised their plans; Zhang 2023 (N=622) is not a premortem study.
agent_test: Treat premortem as a hypothesis generator only.

claim: The premortem benefit may come from framing direction or safe dissent, not hindsight: a student poster found forward 'promortem' more confident in Exp 1 but a null in Exp 2. Gap search: the one LLM direction control (InvThink inverse vs forward SFT, Qwen-2.5-7B) was a null; Hill 2012 shows listing any scenario set inflates probability (unpacking), a rival mechanism.
agent_test: Contrast forward-success vs backward-failure prompts.

claim: Known outcomes raise judged probability (hindsight bias, Fischhoff 1975); the premortem uses the same certainty effect, and the one reliable debiaser is considering how alternatives could be true.
agent_test: Prompt the agent to argue the alternative outcome before it judges.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not help and often hurts reasoning: GPT-3.5 CommonsenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5.
agent_test: Compare self-critique with and without an external check at equal tokens.

claim: Models are poor at locating reasoning errors (GPT-4 52.87 on BIG-Bench Mistake) but fix them well when told the location.
agent_test: Give the agent a code-found error location versus asking it to find one.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Reflection helps when a failure signal exists or the reflection is rich: Reflexion HumanEval 91 vs 80; Renze re-answers improve with richer reflection; both condition on being told the first try failed.
agent_test: Tell the agent only that it failed (Retry) vs a richer premortem; check what the premortem adds beyond Retry.

claim: External or tool-verified critique beats self-only critique: CRITIC +7.7 F1; about 12% of GPT-4 plans executable alone; the LLM's own criticisms often miss.
agent_test: Premortem causes must be checked by a tool or code before the agent acts on them.

claim: Verification with the draft hidden works best (CoVe FACTSCORE 55.9 to 71.4 factor+revise); backward verification gives small gains (+2.33%).
agent_test: Run premortem causes as independent check questions with the draft hidden.

claim: Self-Refine reports about 20% absolute gain on open-ended tasks but 0 on GPT-3.5 math and +0.2 on code optimization; it conflicts with the pessimistic results only for style tasks.
agent_test: Split tasks by verifiability when testing critique.

claim: LLMs are poor at post-failure attribution: Who&When best 53.5% agent, 14.2% step; MAST failure rates 41 to 86.7% with verification modes common. Hindsight attribution is hard, so prospective failure generation is probably harder.
agent_test: Measure the agent's causal-step accuracy on logged failures.

claim: Machine-generated adversarial cases scale but collapse in diversity (Perez 2022: 78% of RL cases contained 'invisible'); a premortem sampler needs a diversity constraint.
agent_test: Count distinct failure categories per 10 sampled premortems.

claim: Critique assistance helps humans find flaws (+50% flaws, Saunders 2022; CriticGPT preferred 63% and 80%) but critics hallucinate and nitpick.
agent_test: Count real vs hallucinated flaws in premortem output.

claim: Veinott and Lehman 2024 compares student failure reasons with ChatGPT-4 reasons qualitatively; the abstract was read but no result is reported on it, and the full text is behind a login wall. The question 'did LLM causes match human causes' is unanswered.
agent_test: Read that paper; run an own premortem ablation.

claim: Forward simulation of action outcomes with an LLM world model gave +34.1% relative on VisualWebArena; reverse-thinking training gave +13.53%. Both are relatives of the premortem, not failure-frame prompts.
agent_test: Compare simulate-failure vs simulate-success per action at equal tokens.

claim: Models can estimate P(True) for their own answers, so a confidence shift could serve as the outcome measure for an LLM premortem. Gap search found no study that measures P(True) after a premortem.
agent_test: Measure P(True) shift and accuracy before and after a premortem prompt.

claim: Hill 2012 (N=32 search-and-rescue planners) is not a premortem study. It shows that unpacking the 'outside the area' scenarios raised that probability, F(1,28)=4.753, p=.038, and only 11 of 32 showed the effect. Reviews that cite it as premortem evidence are wrong.
agent_test: none
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A structured failure-first prompt (InvThink: list harms, analyse, then answer) beat a plain safety instruction at similar token counts on judged harmfulness (2.19 vs 2.62 vs 3.22 zero-shot, 1-5 scale, LLM judges). Safety task only.
agent_test: Run failure-list vs plain risk-list vs retry arms at equal tokens on reasoning items; score by code-confirmed flaws.

claim: The only LLM test of failure vs success direction (InvThink SFT, matched tokens) found no difference: both reached safety rate 1.000; harmfulness 1.23 vs 1.01. Both arms collapsed to refusal, so power was low.
agent_test: Include a forward success-scenario arm at equal tokens in every premortem test.

claim: Trained pre-mortem methods improve math accuracy by about 4-6 points over GRPO (AUGUR abstract: +5.01, +4.28, +5.66), and InvThink SFT+RL kept or raised reasoning (avg 0.61 to 0.63, single seed). No prompt-only equal-token evidence on reasoning accuracy exists.
agent_test: Do not expect a prompt-only premortem to raise accuracy; test it.

claim: Backward planning from the goal beats forward planning on motivation and performance, mainly for goals that are complex to plan (Park, Lu, Hedgcock 2017); numbers unread and a corrigendum exists.
agent_test: Test a backward-from-end-state step on hard items only.

claim: Game teams (n=68, 10 teams) found 17.8 failure reasons and 16.7 mitigations on average but few revised their plans; the weak link is acting on found causes, not finding them.
agent_test: Force and score a plan-revision step after any premortem listing.

claim: Self-certified 'verified' labels from agents gave no benefit; harness-audited verification improved downstream diagnosis by +0.114 [0.019, 0.208] (n=55 paired) at some cost in true-rule recall. Supports keeping only tool-confirmed causes.
agent_test: Keep only causes a code or tool check confirms; compare with unverified causes.

claim: A human-review study found a what-if failure prompt was rated more helpful than an assumptions check but did not measure better, and combining both may hurt (N=214).
agent_test: Judge premortem arms by caught flaws, not by perceived usefulness; do not stack prompts without testing.
